- When sentiment is high (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots in next period; apply downward correction of 1–3% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) over 3–5 days, model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for potential rebound.
- Model frequently underpredicts in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or negative — adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% for first 5 days.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive, model lags in adjusting — forecast should be adjusted 1–2 days ahead of sentiment change.
- If model shows strong upward trend but true outcome shows mean reversion within 10–15 days, reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in next 5–7 days.
- For sentiment history with alternating highs/lows, model tends to overfit recent sentiment — dampen forecast by 0.5–1.0% if sentiment is volatile or inconsistent.
